messages.text: Leeds and Rangers co-owner York arrested

metadata.summary: Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
metadata.content: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences By Adrian Kajumba and Sahil Jaidka Tuesday 25 August 2026 08:59, UK Image: Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools. Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors. York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offence

metadata.summary: Iconic rugby league player Sir Billy Boston has died aged 92.
metadata.content: Sir Billy Boston: Trailblazing rugby league player dies aged 92 | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to content Sir Billy Boston: Trailblazing rugby league player dies aged 92 Trailblazing rugby league player Sir Billy Boston has died at the age of 92; He was the first ever rugby league player to receive a knighthood, ending a 130-year wait for such an honour; He was also the first Black player to represent Great Britain Tuesday 25 August 2026 10:54, UK Image: Sir Billy Boston - 1934-2026 Iconic rugby league player Sir Billy Boston has died aged 92. Back in June 2025, Boston received rugby league's first ever knighthood, ending a 130-year wait for such an honour. Boston blazed a trail for Black sports stars during the 1950s and 1960s, making 488 appearances for Wigan and finishing his career with a British-record 571 tries. Image: Legendary rugby league star Billy Boston played in six Challenge Cup Finals at Wembley He also became the first non-white player to represent Great Britain on a Lions tour in 1954, scoring 36 tries in 18 appearances in Australia and New Zealand, and featuring in a total of 31 international Test matches. Boston made a try-scoring debut for Wigan against Barrow in November 1953, and by the time he left the club in 1968, he had played in six Challenge Cup finals at Wembley, featuring on the winning side in 1958, 1959 and 1965. Not pundit analysis, but the thoughts of Chelsea head coach Sonia Bompastor to Sky Sports ahead of the new WSL season. And despite the hint of cliché, it works. There has been plenty upheaval over the last two years, starting with Bompastor replacing Emma Hayes. Then, there was the shock departure of Paul Green as head of women's football in February.
